subject: Hosting qualification: data residency and region availability for Celestia Health
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elin Sørensen <elin@celestiahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: residency & region constraints — next steps

Hi Elin / Mikael,

Thanks for taking time earlier — useful call. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can propose the right hosting path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Call recap (short):
- Use case: conversational triage + PHI annotations for EU-based patients (primary regulation: GDPR + local data residency).
- Current preference: keep all patient data within EU; team asked about Germany-only residency and Singapore fallback for APAC users.
- Procurement: security questionnaire in progress; procurement will need SLA and onboarding timeline.

Key clarifying questions:
1) Is an absolute constraint that both inference and stored logs must never leave EU? Or is processing in EU sufficient with encrypted/limited telemetry allowed to cross regions?
2) Do you need an on-prem option (air-gapped) for any portion, or would a VPC/private deployment inside your GCP tenancy be acceptable?
3) Expected QPS and peak concurrency for the triage endpoint (helps recommend Dedicated vs Hosted).

Proposed next steps (we can action once you confirm answers above):
- Vivek to scope VPC deployment options for Frankfurt (de-centralized KMS options + estimated lead time).
- Ben to produce Hosted vs Dedicated cost/latency estimate for your QPS profile.
- Send SOC2 + onboarding checklist (attached) and open a shared HubSpot/Drive folder for questionnaires.

Do you have 30 minutes Thursday or Friday for a quick technical follow-up with Vivek?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
(attachment: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf)
(attachment: VPC_onboarding_checklist.xlsx)

From: Elin Sørensen <elin@celestiahealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency & region constraints — next steps

Hi Lauren,

Thanks — that matches our notes. Quick answers:
- Residency requirement: inference and any persisted patient-identifiable logs must remain in the EU. Aggregated, anonymized telemetry is OK to cross regions but must be encrypted-at-rest and we need a KMS integration.
- On-prem: not at this stage; VPC in our GCP tenancy is preferred but we may discuss on-prem in later phases.
- Expected load: baseline 20 requests/sec, bursts up to 120 req/s for short windows.

Other asks from procurement:
- Lead time estimate for a Private VPC deployment in Frankfurt (we have a standard change request window of ~6 weeks).
- Draft SLA and estimated monthly cost for a Dedicated pool sized for the burst profile.
- Confirmation that cross-region routing fallback (to another EU region) can be forced off for strict data paths.

I can do Thursday 14:00–15:00 CET for the technical follow-up.

Thanks,
Elin
Head of Platform Security | Celestia Health
elin@celestiahealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elin Sørensen <elin@celestiahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency & region constraints — next steps

Hi Elin — thanks for the quick clarifications. Short answers and what we'll deliver ahead of Thursday's call: 

1) EU residency enforcement
- We support two strong patterns: Private VPC (Redwood Private) deployed into your GCP project in the Frankfurt region (eu-west3) which ensures all inference and persisted logs never leave your tenancy; or Dedicated capacity in our Frankfurt cluster with tenancy-level data isolation (logs can be configured to remain in EU-only storage).
- For strict no-cross-border rules, Private VPC in your project is the recommended path; we can disable cross-region failover in routing policy.

2) KMS / encryption
- We have KMS integrations for GCP KMS and AWS KMS. In the Private VPC flow we point to your KMS keys; in Dedicated we can support customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption. Details in the attached checklist.

3) Capacity recommendation
- Baseline 20 req/s with bursts to 120 req/s: recommended approach is a small Dedicated pool with autoscaling burst policy + prefix caching for common prompts. That gives predictable latency and cost control during bursts. Estimated lead time:
  - Hosted API: immediate onboarding (no residency guarantee for Germany-only).
  - Dedicated (Frankfurt): ~2–4 weeks for capacity reservation + testing.
  - Private VPC (in your GCP): ~4–8 weeks depending on networking approvals (matches your 6-week change window).

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf; VPC_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (contains KMS, firewall rules, peering examples).

Deliverables before the Thursday call:
- Detailed Dedicated vs Private cost/latency estimate for 20/120 req/s (I'll send a one-pager).
- A short runbook showing how we lock routing to EU-only (for procurement/legal).
- Vivek will bring the technical checklist for VPC peering and IAM mappings.

See you Thursday 14:00 CET.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
